KISS ceiling: #5783 Prefer-A Bound 6280270826 (Thin Fail-Closed #3265 / writing-bar #3368)

## In plain English

Same-day directive upgrade to a fresh @deftai/directive-runtime pin fails pnpm install / frozen CI for up to 24h because pnpm-workspace.yaml minimumReleaseAgeExclude keeps the old runtime version (or gains a second exact entry). pnpm 11 honours the first matching package entry, so the new exclude is inert. Prefer-A makes the version-changing upgrade path **replace** any prior @deftai/directive-runtime@* AgeExclude entries with exactly one @deftai/directive-runtime@<target> entry. Unrelated excludes stay untouched. Naming/docs are footnotes under #5783.

## Draft remedy sketch

1. After successful version-changing upgrade PM add (pnpm workspace roots), upsert pnpm-workspace.yaml minimumReleaseAgeExclude: remove every existing @deftai/directive-runtime@* exact entry, then ensure exactly one @deftai/directive-runtime@<targetVersion> entry (create the key/list if absent).
2. Leave non-runtime AgeExclude rows alone; do not widen to a bare-name @deftai/directive-runtime exclude; npm-only / non-workspace paths that lack the file stay no-ops.
3. Bookend/unit regression: fixture starts with @old, upgrade target @new → yaml has exactly one runtime exclude and it is @new; dual-entry / leave-old shapes fail the assertion.
4. CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

## Reject (draft)

- Relying on manual post-upgrade yaml edits as the standing fix.
- Patching pnpm itself or waiting on upstream first-match semantics.
- Bare-name AgeExclude for the runtime (widens maturity gate).
- Rewriting unrelated vite/brace-expansion/postcss/source-map-js excludes.

## file_scope (lean)

- packages/cli/src/bookends.ts and/or packages/cli/src/pm.ts (post-add upsert call site)
- new/adjacent helper + tests under packages/cli (or shared core helper if already the yaml owner)
- CHANGELOG.md

Verification: read the issue body and the three named comments only; used the recorded SHA-pinned read path. The pinned workspace contains the old runtime exclusion. In [bookends.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/f0b2a3623a6be6ab2952bcafca0c8114b2b058cf/packages/cli/src/bookends.ts#L1218-L1246), successful PM add proceeds to pin/installation checks and setup without exclusion normalization. [pm.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/f0b2a3623a6be6ab2952bcafca0c8114b2b058cf/packages/cli/src/pm.ts#L710-L720) delegates add to pnpm and interprets its exit status; it supplies no exclusion writer. This supports the missing-bookend premise. The pnpm 11 first-match behavior remains the issue author's reported observation; I did not independently execute pnpm.

### C1 — sharpens-framing: exercise the post-add duplicate input

Evidence: the issue's failing artifact already contains both old and target entries, whereas draft item 3 explicitly starts its fixture with only old. The existing runPmAdd injection seam allows the regression to model pnpm appending target before the proposed normalization runs.

Failure mode: a helper that replaces the first old entry with target passes an old-only fixture but produces target,target when pnpm has already appended target. Likewise, an early return upon finding target leaves old,target unchanged. Both violate the draft's exactly-one postcondition.

Disposition: retain the mechanism and strengthen the existing regression to have successful PM add leave old,target before normalization; assert exactly one target afterward and preservation of unrelated entries. Keep the old-only case too. This is a test-input clarification within item 3, not a new subsystem or a longer Bound.

### C2 — footnote: reuse the existing mutation boundary

The upgrade already checks dry-run, approval, and plan invalidation before PM add; pnpm-workspace.yaml is already fingerprinted by planCriticalRelPaths. Place the upsert inside that admitted version-changing pnpm path. These existing controls cover the pre-mutation shared-file boundary; no new approval or coordination mechanism is warranted.

Road not taken: a bare-package exemption is simpler and survives future upgrades, but deliberately exempts every runtime version. The exact target upsert preserves the draft's narrower exception. A requirement to support multiple simultaneous runtime pins would change that tradeoff; none is present in this envelope.

Critic complete; returning to the parent for Round-1 synthesis.

Mandatory reads only (issue body, draft 6357397661, Stop 1 6357397898, panel-deposit 6357403601, design-critique Critic method + Bound thinness #3265 + writing-bar #3368). Pin-read at dispatch-sha: packages/cli/src/bookends.ts (runUpgrade / post-add), packages/cli/src/pm.ts, pnpm-workspace.yaml. No post-ceiling thread input; no product edits.

## Inventory (pin-read)

- pnpm-workspace.yaml already carries minimumReleaseAgeExclude with exact @deftai/directive-runtime@0.127.0 plus unrelated vite/brace-expansion/postcss/source-map-js rows; package.json pins @deftai/directive-runtime 0.127.0 and packageManager pnpm@11.8.0.
- packages/cli/src/bookends.ts runUpgrade versionChange path calls runPmExactAdd then pin/install verify then handOffSetup/migrate — no AgeExclude read or write.
- packages/cli/src/pm.ts knows isPnpmWorkspaceRoot / buildPmExactAddArgs (-w) / plan-critical pnpm-workspace.yaml fingerprint; no AgeExclude helper.
- Repo-wide git grep for minimumReleaseAgeExclude under *.ts at the pin hits only the yaml file (no Directive writer). Stop 1 P2 matches: gap is missing upsert, not a mis-aimed append helper.
- Existing thinner gate pattern elsewhere: isFrameworkRepoRoot in packages/core/src/check/context.ts (packages/cli + biome.json + Taskfile.yml).

Prefer-A replace-not-append for version-changing upgrade is the right primary clear path for P1–P3 under KISS #5783. It cannot bind as written because of create-if-absent consumer injection; timing should move pre-add.

### F1 — blocks-the-design: create-if-absent injects AgeExclude into consumer workspaces

Evidence: Draft remedy sketch limb 1 upserts on all pnpm workspace roots and explicitly "create the key/list if absent". Limb 2 only no-ops when the workspace file is absent (npm-only / non-workspace). Tip AgeExclude is maintainer supply-chain policy on the framework checkout; consumer pnpm workspaces commonly have pnpm-workspace.yaml with no minimumReleaseAgeExclude and no prior @deftai/directive-runtime@* exclude.

Failure mode: every consumer directive upgrade on a pnpm workspace root that lacks the key (or lacks a runtime exact entry) gains a Directive-authored maturity-gate bypass for the runtime. That widens authority over consumer manifests beyond the observed framework-repo leave-old / dual-entry pain (injection / shared-state lens).

Disposition consequence: Prefer-A cannot bind create-if-absent / ensure-one when no prior exact @deftai/directive-runtime@* AgeExclude entry exists. Gate the upsert: when ≥1 prior exact runtime AgeExclude entries exist, remove them and write exactly one @deftai/directive-runtime@<targetVersion>; otherwise no-op (leave unrelated rows and absent keys untouched). That still closes P1–P3 on the repro without consumer policy injection. Road-not-taken: hard isFrameworkRepoRoot-only gate — thinner blast radius on paper; flip only if prior-entry repos that are not framework roots must not be healed (they should). Prior-entry is the thinner fail-closed association.

### F2 — sharpens-framing: replace before runPmExactAdd, not only after success

Evidence: Issue body — pnpm 11 honours the first matching package AgeExclude entry; with @…@0.127.0 first, @…@0.128.0 is inert and frozen install fails ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION. Tip yaml lists only @0.127.0. Draft limb 1 schedules upsert "After successful version-changing upgrade PM add". runUpgrade performs the add at the versionChange branch before any yaml heal would run under that wording.

Failure mode: post-only upsert leaves the same-day add (and any install that runs under first-match-old) gated by the stale first entry. Observed upgrade exit 0 then failed frozen install is one failure shape; first-match-old during add is the adjacent shape the Bound must not leave optional.

Disposition consequence: Bound can still Prefer-A replace-not-append, but the call site is the version-changing upgrade path immediately before runPmExactAdd when the F1 prior-entry gate is true. Regression: fixture with @old → upgrade target @new yields exactly one runtime exclude @new (dual-entry / leave-old fail); assert relative to the add, not only a late post-success rewrite. CHANGELOG limb stays.

### F3 — footnote: "appends" titles a missing writer

Evidence: pin-read shows no minimumReleaseAgeExclude writer in packages/cli (or other *.ts). Stop 1 already names the missing writer. Failure mode: none for the remedy once F1/F2 land. Disposition: omit from Bound; keep replace-upsert framing.

### F4 — footnote: install/repair first-pin keep-out under KISS

Evidence: Stop 1 pains and issue Expected target version-changing upgrade; runInstall also PM-adds with no AgeExclude heal. Failure mode: same-day first install on a repo that already has a stale runtime AgeExclude is theoretically adjacent. Disposition: leftover/footnote unless bind evidence appears; do not grow Prefer-A Bound (#3265 / #3368).

## Verdict

Refute Prefer-A draft 6357397661 as written (F1 blocks). Accept the replace-not-append core once Bound gates on prior exact runtime AgeExclude entries (no create-if-absent) and performs that replace before PM add (F2). Reject list and CHANGELOG limb survive. Empty road-not-taken beyond F1 steelman.

Verdict: Prefer-A binds. Replace-not-append is the right primary clear path and the right file. One `blocks-the-design` on where the mechanism is sited; the rest sharpen the limb wording.

## Re-verification (pin-read at f0b2a362)

- **P1 confirmed as state, not as cause.** `pnpm-workspace.yaml` at the pin carries exactly one runtime row, `- '@deftai/directive-runtime@0.127.0'`, while the tip commit is the v0.128.0 release. Root `package.json` devDeps also still pin `@deftai/directive-runtime: 0.127.0`, so pin and exclude are mutually consistent at the pin; the dual-entry shape is produced during the upgrade run, not committed. The exclude row was last written by `cc4bd5db5 chore(ovpr): Phase 10 self-host pin`, i.e. by hand, never by a Directive mechanism.
- **P2 confirmed, and stronger than stated.** A pin-read grep for minimumReleaseAge / AgeExclude across `packages/`, `content/`, `docs/`, `skills/`, `templates/` returns **zero** hits. Directive owns no reader, no writer, no fixture. The only launcher touches of `pnpm-workspace.yaml` are read-only: `isPnpmWorkspaceRoot` (`existsSync`, pm.ts:571) and `fileDigest` via `planCriticalRelPaths` (pm.ts:486-496), which already lists the file as plan-critical. The remedy would be the launcher's first *write* to that file.
- **Policy source.** `minimumReleaseAge` itself is set nowhere in the repo (no `.npmrc` at the pin; the yaml sets only packages / overrides / allowBuilds / minimumReleaseAgeExclude), so the gate is pnpm 11 default behaviour and the committed exclude list is the only lever. Prefer-A is aimed at the right surface.

## Inventory

`packages/cli` declares an empty `dependencies` map and bundles to a single `dist/bin.js`. There is no YAML parser in the launcher and no existing yaml writer to reuse, so any upsert helper is a hand-rolled, dependency-free text edit. That constraint belongs in the Bound, not in the implementer's discovery.

## blocks-the-design

**Siting the upsert in upgrade's version-change branch leaves the same failure reachable on the install path and strands a half-finished upgrade with no repair route.**

Evidence (pin-read): `runPmExactAdd` has three call sites, not one. `runFirstInstall` (bookends.ts:625), `runRepair` (bookends.ts:741, gated on `needsPmRestore`), `runUpgrade` (bookends.ts:1220). All three add an exact `@deftai/directive-runtime` version into a possibly-pnpm-workspace root. Draft step 1 scopes the upsert to "after successful version-changing upgrade PM add", which covers one of them.

Failure mode 1 - install day. `directive install` into a pnpm workspace pins a runtime younger than the cutoff with no Directive-written exclude at all. Same `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` on the next frozen install, and the draft's mechanism never runs.

Failure mode 2 - stranding. In `runUpgrade` the add succeeds at :1220, pin and installed-package verification pass, then `handOffSetup` returns non-zero at :1257 and the function returns. The repo now holds the new pin in `package.json` plus lockfile and the old exclude row - exactly the broken state in the issue. The printed recovery is to re-run `directive upgrade --yes`, but pin now equals target, so `versionChange` is false and control takes the equal-version path (:1313), which performs no PM add. A mechanism gated on "version-changing PM add" can never repair what a mid-upgrade failure created. `directive repair` only adds when `needsPmRestore`, so it is not a dependable repair either. The remaining route is hand-editing the yaml, which the draft's own Reject list rules out as the standing fix.

Disposition consequence: the Bound limb should name the **shared post-add seam** - one upsert reached by every `runPmExactAdd` caller, invoked immediately after the add and before the setup/migrate hand-off - rather than `runUpgrade`'s version-change branch. This is thinner than the draft, not thicker: one site instead of a branch-specific patch, and it stays a single mechanism sentence under #3265. If the panel keeps upgrade-only scope, say so explicitly and book install-day and stranded repos as leftover-pain, rather than leaving them implied as covered.

## sharpens-framing

**"Create the key/list if absent" writes supply-chain policy into projects that configured none, and nothing ever prunes it.**

Evidence: the draft's no-op rule keys on file presence, the same `existsSync` predicate `isPnpmWorkspaceRoot` already uses (pm.ts:571). File presence is not policy presence: a pnpm workspace root that never set a maturity gate would gain a Directive-authored `minimumReleaseAgeExclude:` key. Failure mode: Directive writes a supply-chain policy surface the project did not opt into, and since no removal path prunes it (`runPmRemove` touches package.json and lockfiles only, pm.ts:733-768), the row outlives the dependency and drifts stale permanently. Consequence: narrow the limb to update-if-present - rewrite the runtime rows when the key already exists, otherwise no-op silently. That also keeps the mechanism honest about coverage: it fixes projects that configured the gate here, and claims nothing about projects that configure it elsewhere.

## sharpens-framing

**The Bound must name the edit strategy; comment loss or an unparseable file is a worse outcome than the bug being fixed.**

Evidence: the pin's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` carries the Dependabot rationale comments for #1989 / #5737 / #1717 inline above `overrides` and `allowBuilds`, and the single runtime row is quoted (`- '@deftai/directive-runtime@0.127.0'`) because a plain YAML scalar cannot begin with an at-sign. Failure modes: a parse-and-restringify helper silently drops every one of those security comments on the first upgrade; a hand-rolled line writer - which the zero-dep inventory above forces - that emits the row unquoted produces a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` that no longer parses, converting a 24h install failure into a permanently broken workspace. Consequence: one clause in the Bound (line-scoped edit of the existing list, quoted entry, no YAML round-trip), and step 3's regression asserts comment preservation and quoting next to the single-entry assertion, not entry count alone.

## sharpens-framing

**Plan and `--dry-run` do not mention the file the command would now rewrite.**

Evidence: `runUpgrade` presents the plan, fingerprints (:1162), then honours `--dry-run` (:1164) before any write; the upgrade plan fields in `plan-present.ts` (:435-458) name the pin change only. Failure mode: `--dry-run` reports "no changes made" while the real run rewrites a supply-chain policy file, understating the blast radius for the one file a reviewer is most likely watching. Consequence: name the yaml row in the presented plan and dry-run lines when the upsert will fire.

## footnote

The first-entry-wins reading of pnpm 11 comes from one manual repro and is not checkable under this arc's pin-read verification path. It does not need to be: replacing to exactly one entry is correct under first-wins, last-wins, or match-all. Keep it out of the CHANGELOG and commit message as an asserted upstream fact - describe the Directive-side behaviour (one row per package, equal to the pin) and leave pnpm's matching order unclaimed.

## footnote

Helper naming and any docs row stay footnotes under the #5783 Prefer-A Bound.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered - the change writes a supply-chain gate from a CLI-supplied value. `--target-version` is already narrowed by `validateTargetVersionSpec` before it reaches the add (bookends.ts:1039), and the upsert consumes that same validated string, so no new untrusted-input surface opens. The residual is the quoting hazard above, which is a correctness control on the writer, not an input control.

## Road not taken

Prune-only: let pnpm's own add-time append write the new row, and have Directive delete only stale non-target `@deftai/directive-runtime` rows. Strictly thinner, and it matches the repro, where pnpm did append the new row unprompted.

Steelman: if pnpm appends on every `pnpm add` of an age-gated package, prune-only is the smaller mechanism and leaves the write to the tool that owns the file.

What flips it: that append is upstream behaviour this arc cannot verify under pin-read, and it is conditional at minimum on the policy being active at add time. If it does not fire, prune-only deletes the old row and leaves none - a harder failure than today's. Idempotent upsert is the fail-closed choice and costs one line more in the writer.

## In plain English

When a project already lists exact @deftai/directive-runtime@* rows under minimumReleaseAgeExclude, every successful exact runtime PM-add path (upgrade / install / repair) must leave exactly one quoted @deftai/directive-runtime@<target> entry — replace before add so the add is not gated by a stale first-match, and upsert again after add so a pnpm-appended dual entry collapses. Never create the AgeExclude key or a first runtime exclude where none existed. Unrelated excludes and inline rationale comments stay. Plan/dry-run name the yaml rewrite when the upsert will fire. CHANGELOG records it.

## Bound remedy

- relieves: P1 — Prior-entry gated replace-not-append: if pnpm-workspace.yaml has ≥1 exact @deftai/directive-runtime@* minimumReleaseAgeExclude entries, remove those runtime exacts and ensure exactly one quoted @deftai/directive-runtime@<targetVersion> entry; no create-if-absent / no ensure-key; leave unrelated exclude rows; line-scoped edit (no YAML round-trip that drops #1989/#5737/#1717 rationale comments).
- relieves: P2 — Shared pre+post runPmExactAdd seam: invoke that upsert from every runPmExactAdd caller (runUpgrade version-change, runFirstInstall, runRepair needsPmRestore) immediately before add when the P1 gate is true, and again immediately after successful add (idempotent dual-entry collapse) before setup/migrate handoff; dry-run/plan disclosure when the upsert will fire.
- relieves: P3 — Regression + CHANGELOG: fixtures cover old-only and old+target pre-normalization → exactly one @new afterward; unrelated rows + comment preservation + quoted entry asserted; dual-entry/leave-old shapes fail; CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

## Accept-into-contract (Round-1)

- Grok F1: prior-entry gate; no create-if-absent consumer injection (blocks draft as written).
- Grok F2: replace before runPmExactAdd when gate true.
- Codex C1: post-add dual-entry (old,target) regression / idempotent collapse.
- Claude blocks: shared seam across install/repair/upgrade (not upgrade-only); line-scoped quoted edit; plan/dry-run disclosure.
- Claude/Grok footnotes: first-match order unclaimed; helper naming/docs footnote; install-day absent-key keep-out under prior-entry gate.

## Reject

- Create-if-absent / ensure-key AgeExclude on consumer workspaces that had no runtime exact exclude.
- Bare-name @deftai/directive-runtime AgeExclude (widens maturity gate).
- Upgrade-only siting that leaves install/repair and stranded mid-upgrade unrepaired.
- YAML parse-and-restringify that drops workspace rationale comments.
- Patching pnpm upstream or manual post-upgrade yaml as the standing fix.
- Rewriting unrelated vite/brace-expansion/postcss/source-map-js excludes.

## pain-P1 — relieved on the forward path; **blocking** gap on the already-broken population

The remedy fires only where `runPmExactAdd` fires. At the pin that is three sites and no more (`git grep` at `f0b2a3623`, non-test: bookends.ts:625, :741, :1220). A repo that is already in the issue's end state — new pin, lockfile and installed package agreeing, stale or dual runtime row in the yaml — reaches none of them:

- `directive upgrade` → `versionChange` is false (`versionOrd !== 0` fails, not oldStyle), so control takes the equal-version path at :1313, which performs no PM add.
- `directive repair` → `lockOk` and `installedOk` are both true, so `needsPmRestore` is false (:696) and the add at :741 is skipped.
- `directive install` on an existing exact pin routes to `runRepair` (:531/:535), i.e. the same no-op.

So the remedy heals the yaml on the *next* version bump and never heals the state the issue actually reports. The Bound's Reject list already claims this ground — "Upgrade-only siting that leaves install/repair and stranded mid-upgrade unrepaired" — but the P2 limb re-gates repair behind `needsPmRestore`, which is exactly the condition that is false whenever the yaml row is the only thing wrong. Reject clause and mechanism disagree.

Disposition consequence: ungate the repair-side upsert — run the P1 prior-entry-gated upsert on every `runRepair` that passes approval and the plan check, not only when `needsPmRestore`. That is thinner than it sounds: repair's charter is drift reconciliation, the yaml row becomes Directive-owned drift the moment this lands, repair already presents a plan and already honours dry-run, and no new call site or file enters `file_scope`. If the panel prefers to keep repair add-gated, say so and book "repos already holding a stale runtime AgeExclude" as leftover-pain explicitly, and drop the third Reject bullet, rather than leaving the population implied as covered.

Shared pre+post seam across the three callers is the correct reach and `deps.runPmAdd` (:623, :739, :1218) gives the implementer the seam without new plumbing.

The P1 limb says "line-scoped edit" and "leave unrelated exclude rows", which under-specifies the anchor. At the pin, the string `@deftai/directive-runtime` occurs **twice** in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: once as `'@deftai/directive-runtime': true` under `allowBuilds`, once as `- '@deftai/directive-runtime@0.127.0'` under `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`. The listed fixtures (old-only, old+target) assert the postcondition of the *whole* path. Two of the Bound's own accepted findings survive those assertions unbroken:

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

`directive upgrade --target-version <ver>` **appends** a new `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` entry for `@deftai/directive-runtime@<ver>` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and keeps the old version's entry. In our test, pnpm 11 honoured only the first entry for the package, which is the old one, so the new exclusion had no effect. For the first 24h after a release, `pnpm install` (and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI) therefore fails.

## Repro (upgrade 0.127.0 → 0.128.0 on deftai/directive master `f0b2a3623`, pnpm 11.8.0)

Upgrade output (exit 0) changed `pnpm-workspace.yaml` to:

```yaml
minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
  ...
  - '@deftai/directive-runtime@0.127.0'
  - '@deftai/directive-runtime@0.128.0'
```

Then:

```
$ pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
✗ Lockfile failed supply-chain policy check (173 entries)
[ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION] 1 lockfile entries failed verification:
  @deftai/directive-runtime@0.128.0 was published at 2026-10-23T03:15:37.000Z, within the minimumReleaseAge cutoff
```

`pnpm config get minimumReleaseAgeExclude` listed both entries. Removing the stale `@0.127.0` line, so the list has a single `@deftai/directive-runtime@0.128.0` entry, fixed it:

```
✓ Lockfile passes supply-chain policies (173 entries)
Done in 1s using pnpm v11.8.0
```

## Expected

The upgrader **replaces** the previous `@deftai/directive-runtime@<old>` exclude entry with the target version. Alternatively it could write a single merged selector, but replacing is simpler, since the old version is the outgoing pin. The result should be one entry per package, so a same-day pin bump installs locally and in frozen CI installs.

Part of the pin/master skew tracked in #5848.

_Filed by Grok Bot (Engineering) for @MScottAdams_
